full_judgment: 2. This arises from Title Suit No.201 of 1963 of the 3rd Court of Munsif, Comilla. The suit land, which appertained to C.S. Plots Nos. 675 and 678 of Mouza Chatura, belonged to defendant No 2. Delaney Estate which possessed it in khas. The plaintiff purchased it by a registered kabala dated 1, August 1959, went into possession and made some constructions including pucca boundary pillars. But on 12 August 1963 defendantNo.1; the respondent before us, forcibly dispossessed him from this land setting up a claim of title on the basis of purchase under a registered kabala dated 11 July 1963 from one Rabi Dasi, daughter of one Biman Dasi. Defendant No.1 claimed that Biman Dasi took lease of 10 decimals of land including the suit land from the Delaney Estate by executing kabuliyat in the year 1935 and that after possessing it for many years she gifted it to her daughter, Rabi Dasi, by a deed of gift dated 6-9-62. The lease of Biman Dasi, it was alleged by defendant No.1, was for 10 decimals of land, but in the lease-deed the area was wrongly stated to be 'one' decimal instead of 10 decimals; nevertheless, the lease was acted upon in respect of the whole area and the land was all along in possession of the lessee. The plaintiff denied tae alleged mis-description in the lease-deed and led evidence to show that on a previous occasion the vendor of defendant No.1 had dispossessed the Delaney Estate from the suit land whereupon possession was recovered and title of the landlord was declared by a decree passed in Title Suit No.128 of 1965. Defendant No 1 contended that the suit land covered by the decree in the previous title suit was different from the subject-matter of the instant suit. But a Pleader Commissioner who held a local investigation, submitted a report finding that the lands under both the suits are same and identical.
